name: useradd
description: Low-level command to create an account (requires sudo). By default, it creates neither a home directory nor a password: remember -m, then passwd. On Debian and Ubuntu, adduser is a simpler interactive helper that does all of this automatically.

options.description: Path of the home directory, if it should not be /home/NAME.
Creates a system account (for a service, with no login).

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Login name of the new account (lowercase, no spaces).

examples.explanation: Creates alice with a home directory and bash as her shell.
Creates alice and adds her to the sudo and docker groups.
Creates a system account that cannot log in, to run a service.

dangerNote: Adding someone to the sudo group gives full administrator rights. To change an existing account, use usermod -aG (without -a, the other groups are removed).
